html:
A lighthouse on the island of Pharos at the harbour of Alexandria, built by the Ptolemaic kings and finished under Ptolemy II around 280 BCE. It was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

It was probably over 100 metres tall, among the tallest buildings on Earth for centuries. It rose in three stages, square, then eight sided, then round, with a fire at the top. The Egyptian coast is low and flat, so ships needed a mark to find the harbour. Its architect is named as Sostratus of Cnidus.

It made Alexandria, home of the Library, the great port of the eastern Mediterranean, and its name became the word for lighthouse in several languages, such as French phare and Italian faro. Earthquakes damaged it over the centuries, and by the 14th century it was a ruin. In 1477 the Mamluk sultan Qaitbay built a fort on the site, the Citadel of Qaitbay, partly with its stones. Divers have found blocks from it in the harbour.
